text:
maya_support: ACME reported repeated mid-stream silence for SSE after LTE->WiFi automatic switch. Partial JSON chunks arrive then ~20-35s silent gap, then client FINs. Customer says stream never resumes and they see duplicate partial tokens when they re-open. Attaching short logs below.

streambot: [alert] stream-drop detected: session=acme-01 severity=warning time=2025-09-04T12:03:25Z route=/v1/streams/generate

devon_sre: Got it. Do we have the client keepalive settings + request headers and model used? Also tcpdump or tcp states would help. :eyes:

maya_support: Route: /v1/streams/generate, model: redwood-7b-v2, protocol: text/event-stream (SSE). Client: OkHttp on iOS wrapper, they said readTimeout=0 and they rely on OS. Client keepalive: none application-level, network-level keepalive default.

maya_support: Repro steps from customer: 1) start SSE on LTE with long completion (~60s) 2) toggle WiFi on (auto-switch) 3) after switch, server emits a partial JSON chunk, then nothing for ~22-35s, client eventually closes socket (FIN). When client reconnects they try to resume at last token but server responds new stream (duplicate partial).

maya_support: Snippet from server side access log and a small tcpdump excerpt: ```
12:03:00.123 GET /v1/streams/generate 200 - session=acme-01
12:03:02.340 SSE: data: {"token":"The quick"}
12:03:25.567 TCP FIN from client (192.0.2.10:54321) -> server
```

devon_sre: That FIN after ~23s of silence indicates client-initiated close rather than server RST. Two hypotheses: client OS network migration closes socket, or NAT/proxy in path times out ephemeral mapping and client backoffs. Do we see any proxy hops logged?

maya_support: No intermediate NGW entries for this session. Customer is in APAC on a mobile carrier; they mentioned a corporate VPN on some tests but not the failing ones.

devon_sre: Ask customer to try two quick experiments: 1) set application heartbeat every 10s (simple comment event) to keep socket active across network handoff 2) re-open stream on network-change event instead of relying on OS socket migration. If that reproduces/resolves we can blame client migration behavior.

ricardo_cse: Customer says their app used to rely on OkHttp's transparent connection migration. They see the problem on iOS+carrier combos only, not on Android. They asked if Redwood counts billing for partial chunks that never finished. :money_with_wings:

maya_support: Billing note: we bill by tokens delivered; partial chunks that parse into tokens are billed. I'll confirm edge-case rounding with billing team.

devon_sre: Also suggest they enable our optional header `X-Client-Heartbeat: 10` to send lightweight heartbeats server-side (we'll treat as no-op data events to keep network mappings alive). For server-side recommendations to reduce silent pauses: ensure chunked flush frequency is small, and disable any proxies that buffer SSE. Example nginx config we often share:```
proxy_buffering off;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
proxy_read_timeout 90s;
proxy_send_timeout 90s;
````

maya_support: I asked customer to instrument tcpdump on device and capture the exact moment of SS->WiFi handoff. Also asked for OkHttp version and carrier model. They replied with OkHttp 4.11 and iOS wrapper v1.3.

devon_sre: If tcpdump shows client TCP FIN coincident with interface change, this is client-driven. Two mitigations: - app-level resume (client stores last event id + server supports id resume) - shorter flush interval so more data reaches client before handoff. We don't currently support deterministic resume for long generation streams; plan to propose a resume API.

ricardo_cse: Customer is ok to try the heartbeat header and app-level reconnect for now. They've asked for a short triage doc we can paste into their ticket with exact steps. Can we draft quick repro checklist?

maya_support: Draft checklist sent to customer: 1) enable client heartbeats (10s) or app-level ping events 2) if using OkHttp, set `connectionSpec` to allow clear migration or explicitly close/reopen on network change 3) try toggling WiFi on/off to reproduce, capture tcpdump + server logs 4) send the first and last SSE event ids + any FIN/RST flags.

devon_sre: I'll follow up to see if customer tcpdump shows keepalive probes or ICMP/TCP teardown. If we confirm client FIN on migration, we recommend the app implements immediate re-open and dedupe on server side. Also PR opened to explore 'resume token' API for streams — ETA next sprint. :+1:

maya_support: Customer will test heartbeat header + app reconnect and report back in 24-48h. Marking owner: maya_support, follow-up: devon_sre for any infra traces. :thumbsup:

ricardo_cse: Billing: I confirmed partial chunk token billing is applied; if they want an adjustment we can escalate with billing with session ids.

devon_sre: One last note — if customer uses carrier-level proxies that drop idle connections aggressively, heartbeats are mandatory. Recommend heartbeat <= 15s for mobile carriers.

maya_support: Thanks all, closing loop with customer now.
